purpose: Make durable incidents and lessons influence future runtime decisions without allowing memory to override Root of Trust, evidence rules, or current task evidence.

authority.PROMOTED: active learned guidance; may influence routing and decisions but never overrides Constitution, negative actions, security boundaries, or stronger current evidence
authority.CANDIDATE: hypothesis only; may be considered and tested but must never be represented as established policy or fact
authority.SUPERSEDED: historical anti-regression context only; must not be reactivated without a new evaluated proposal
authority.INCIDENT: historical observed failure evidence; may increase caution and trigger regression checks but is not itself a policy

executionRules: Load memory after a durable task is claimed and before model inference.
Record exactly which lesson and incident IDs were injected into the run.
Record which injected memory IDs the model reports as materially used.
Current evidence outranks historical memory when they conflict.
Candidate lessons must be explicitly labeled CANDIDATE in model context.
Superseded lessons are warnings against accidental reintroduction, not active instructions.
Memory may never authorize repository mutation, production writes, security weakening, Root of Trust mutation, or autonomy escalation.
If relevant memory conflicts with current evidence, return the contradiction in evidence/risks rather than silently choosing one.
A run with no relevant memory must continue normally and record an empty memory selection.
